provenance.review: machine-checked by lab.tools.check_registry (verbatim quotes, sections, ids); content reviewed by Claude where noted in review_notes

draft_notes: Only the supplied document was used. IDs preserve the carriage return in the supplied prefix as JSON \r. Repeated provisions are consolidated where possible: the year definition in Section 3 also covers the exact-length requirement in Section 4.2, and DOY rejection in Section 6.3 covers validation in Section 6.2. Section 1 is purpose text; Section 11 is explicitly non-normative. The 2000-01-01 test vector contradicts Sections 5, 6, and 10: DTI-Day 2451545 yields DY 6809 and DOY 306, not DY 6815 and DOY 26. No precedence rule resolves this contradiction. Section 4.1 names DKP-TIME-001, whereas the document identifies itself as DKP-0-TIME-001; this appears to be a naming inconsistency, not an explicit dependency on another document. The reference implementation supplies Gregorian conversion algorithms but does not specify a timezone, supported input domain, or explicit Gregorian date validation. Python integer annotations are not runtime type checks. SHOULD and MAY are preserved as recommendation and permission rather than mandatory obligations.

requirements.title: Exclude event based time anchors
requirements.quote: Time MUST NOT be anchored to religious, cultural, political, or personal events.
requirements.interpretation: A review must determine whether the time system's anchor belongs to any prohibited event category. The document provides no executable classification of events or definition of anchoring.
requirements.criterion: The time anchor is not a religious, cultural, political, or personal event.
requirements.gap: Neutrality read as an arithmetic origin (DTI-Day = JDN by §3); whether JDN's own origin is neutral is fixed by §3, not judged.
hypotheses_needed: Declare how anchors and prohibited event categories are identified.

requirements.title: Ensure unique date computation
requirements.quote: Any date MUST be uniquely computable from its canonical representation.
requirements.interpretation: Check that each valid canonical representation determines exactly one date using the stated arithmetic and conversion algorithms. Conflicting normative vectors must be reported separately.
requirements.criterion: A valid canonical representation determines exactly one date.

requirements.title: Enable independent index recomputation
requirements.quote: Any record MUST allow independent recomputation of its time index.
requirements.interpretation: Check whether a record supplies enough information to recompute its time index using the protocol. The text does not specify whether storing DTI-Day alone counts as recomputation or whether independent source-date evidence is required.
requirements.criterion: The record permits independent recomputation of its time index.
data_dependencies: record contents and supporting date evidence
hypotheses_needed: Declare whether arithmetic reconstruction from canonical fields is sufficient.

requirements.title: Require governance suitable time units
requirements.quote: Time units MUST be simple, fixed-length, and suitable for legal, financial, and KPI logic.
requirements.interpretation: Fixed length can be tested against unit definitions. Simplicity and suitability for the named uses require judgment because no acceptance criteria are supplied.
requirements.criterion: Time units are simple, fixed-length, and suitable for legal, financial, and KPI logic.
data_dependencies: legal, financial, and KPI use requirements
requirements.gap: The document does not define simplicity or governance suitability.
hypotheses_needed: Declare operational acceptance criteria for simplicity and each named use.

requirements.title: Provide bidirectional civil conversion rules
requirements.quote: Explicit conversion rules to and from civil calendars MUST be provided.
requirements.interpretation: Check for explicit conversion rules in both directions. Gregorian conversion is supplied, but the plural wording could require additional civil calendars whose scope is unspecified.
requirements.criterion: Each civil calendar within the required scope has explicit forward and reverse conversion rules.
requirements.gap: Civil calendars = the Gregorian calendar the text names.
hypotheses_needed: Declare whether Gregorian interoperability alone satisfies this provision.

requirements.title: Define integer civil day indexing
requirements.quote: An integer count of civil days (midnight-to-midnight) in the proleptic Gregorian calendar.
requirements.interpretation: Check that JDN values are integers and correspond to proleptic Gregorian civil days under the supplied conversion algorithm. Applying midnight boundaries to timestamps additionally requires a timezone convention.
requirements.criterion: JDN is an integer index of midnight-to-midnight proleptic Gregorian civil days.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the timezone when checking timestamp-to-day boundaries.

requirements.title: Equate canonical day and JDN
requirements.quote: `DTI-Day = JDN`
requirements.interpretation: Compare the canonical day index with the JDN for the same civil date. They must be identical without an offset.
requirements.criterion: DTI-Day = JDN.

requirements.title: Define consecutive governance year days
requirements.quote: A governance year consisting of exactly 360 consecutive DTI-Days.
requirements.interpretation: Check that each DTI-Year consists of exactly 360 consecutive canonical day indices. This also captures the repeated exact-length obligation in Section 4.2.
requirements.criterion: Each DTI-Year contains exactly 360 consecutive DTI-Days.

requirements.title: Define one based year index
requirements.quote: A 1-based index of a day within a DTI-Year, in the range 1…360.
requirements.interpretation: Check that DOY is an integer ordinal within the year, beginning at 1 and ending at 360.
requirements.criterion: DOY is the 1-based day position and belongs to the integers from 1 through 360.

requirements.title: Use civil day base unit
requirements.quote: - The base temporal unit of DKP-TIME-001 MUST be the civil day.
requirements.interpretation: Check that the protocol's declared base temporal unit is the civil day. The identifier differs from the document ID, so this registry treats the sentence as a requirement of the supplied document.
requirements.criterion: The base temporal unit is the civil day.

requirements.title: Avoid mandatory subday inputs
requirements.quote: - Sub-day units (hours, minutes, seconds) MUST NOT be required by this protocol.
requirements.interpretation: Inspect required inputs and operations to confirm that protocol conformance does not depend on hours, minutes, or seconds. Optional use of such units is not prohibited.
requirements.criterion: No protocol requirement requires hours, minutes, or seconds.

requirements.title: Prohibit governance calendar corrections
requirements.quote: - Leap days, leap years, or corrective rules MUST NOT exist.
requirements.interpretation: Check that DTI year construction contains no leap days, leap years, or corrective rules. The heading scopes this prohibition to governance years; applying it to Gregorian conversion would conflict with Section 10.
requirements.criterion: DTI governance calendar rules contain no leap days, leap years, or corrections.

requirements.title: Determine year boundaries arithmetically
requirements.quote: - Year boundaries MUST be defined purely arithmetically.
requirements.interpretation: Check that boundaries follow the arithmetic mapping in Section 5 without event-based adjustments. Under that mapping, a year begins when the day index is divisible by 360.
requirements.criterion: Year boundaries are determined by the Section 5 arithmetic, with DOY = 1 when DTI-Day mod 360 = 0.

requirements.title: Compute governance year index
requirements.quote: `DY = floor(DTI-Day / 360)`
requirements.interpretation: Recompute DY by mathematical floor division. For negative day indices, truncation toward zero does not implement the specified formula.
requirements.criterion: DY = floor(DTI-Day / 360).

requirements.title: Compute day within governance year
requirements.quote: `DOY = (DTI-Day mod 360) + 1`
requirements.interpretation: Recompute DOY from the remainder plus one. Section 10's Python implementation resolves negative-input remainder behavior to a value from 0 through 359 before adding one.
requirements.criterion: DOY = (DTI-Day mod 360) + 1, using the nonnegative remainder demonstrated by Section 10.

requirements.title: Use canonical date string structure
requirements.quote: `DY<dy>-<doy>`
requirements.interpretation: Check that the serialized date has the literal DY prefix, the year value, a separating hyphen, and the day value. Section 10 supplies the exact canonical formatter.
requirements.criterion: The canonical string equals f"DY{dy}-{doy:03d}" as shown in Section 10.

requirements.title: Constrain canonical date string fields
requirements.quote:
- `<dy>` is a signed integer year index,
- `<doy>` is a zero-padded three-digit day index (001–360).
requirements.interpretation: Check that the year represents a signed integer and that the day uses exactly three digits in the stated range. Signed integer permits negative years; the example and canonical code show that positive years do not require an explicit plus sign.
requirements.criterion: The year field represents an integer; the day field is zero-padded to three digits and ranges from 001 through 360.

requirements.title: Convert Gregorian dates through JDN
requirements.quote:
1.  Compute the JDN using a standard astronomical algorithm.
2.  Set `DTI-Day = JDN`.
3.  Compute `(DY, DOY)` using Section 5.
requirements.interpretation: For a valid Gregorian civil date, compute JDN, copy it to DTI-Day, and apply the Section 5 formulas. Section 10 supplies a canonical astronomical algorithm, making this pipeline executable.
requirements.criterion: Compute JDN with Section 10; require DTI-Day = JDN and DY and DOY to equal the Section 5 results.

requirements.title: Reconstruct day and Gregorian date
requirements.quote:
`DTI-Day = DY × 360 + (DOY − 1)`

3.  Convert `DTI-Day (JDN)` to Gregorian `(year, month, day)`.
requirements.interpretation: After validating DOY, reconstruct the absolute day and apply the inverse Gregorian conversion. This check uses Section 10 for the inverse algorithm.
requirements.criterion: DTI-Day = DY × 360 + (DOY − 1), and the Gregorian output equals jdn_to_gregorian(DTI-Day) from Section 10.

requirements.title: Reject invalid day indices
requirements.quote: - Invalid `DOY` values MUST be rejected.
requirements.interpretation: Check that values outside the integer day-index domain 1 through 360 are rejected. This consolidates Section 6.2's validation step; Section 10 explicitly checks the range but relies on type annotations for integer inputs.
requirements.criterion: Reject DOY unless it is an integer in [1, 360].

requirements.title: Permit negative governance years
requirements.quote: - `DY` MAY be negative.
requirements.interpretation: Negative integer years are permitted by the protocol. A conformance validator must not classify a date as invalid solely because DY is negative.
requirements.criterion: A negative integer DY is not itself a protocol violation.

requirements.title: Prevent derived field overrides
requirements.quote: - Derived fields MUST NOT override `DTI-Day`.
requirements.interpretation: For records containing DTI-Day and derived values, check that processing preserves DTI-Day as the controlling value. Conflicting derived fields cannot change it.
requirements.criterion: Derived fields do not replace or alter the authoritative DTI-Day.

requirements.title: Permit Gregorian readability displays
requirements.quote: - Gregorian dates MAY be shown for human readability.
requirements.interpretation: Displaying Gregorian dates is permitted but not required. Their presence does not grant them authority over the canonical representation.
requirements.criterion: Both displaying and omitting Gregorian dates are permitted.

requirements.title: Include an authoritative date representation
requirements.quote:
- Any authoritative record MUST include:

  - `DTI-Day`, or
requirements.interpretation: Check that every record designated authoritative contains DTI-Day or a complete canonical DY and DOY pair, as specified by the following alternative in the document. The text does not require both representations.
requirements.criterion: An authoritative record includes DTI-Day or canonical (DY, DOY).

requirements.title: Resolve conflicts using canonical day
requirements.quote: - In case of conflict, DTI-Day is authoritative.
requirements.interpretation: When a record's representations disagree and DTI-Day is present, check that the resolved date follows DTI-Day. No conflict-resolution procedure is given for records lacking that field.
requirements.criterion: If DTI-Day conflicts with another date representation, the resolved date is the date represented by DTI-Day.

requirements.title: Recommend canonical day in signatures
requirements.quote:
- Signed records SHOULD store:

  - `DTI-Day` (authoritative),
requirements.interpretation: Check signed records for the recommended authoritative DTI-Day field. The following bullet permits an optional derived DY and DOY pair; absence of DTI-Day is a departure from SHOULD, not automatically a MUST violation.
requirements.criterion: A signed record should store authoritative DTI-Day and may additionally store (DY, DOY) as derived fields.
requirements.gap: A SHOULD: a deviation is reported UNKNOWN, not FAIL.

requirements.title: Reference canonical day during audits
requirements.quote: - Audits and dispute resolution MUST reference `DTI-Day`.
requirements.interpretation: Check audit and dispute-resolution records for a reference to DTI-Day. The protocol does not prescribe a particular storage schema for that reference.
requirements.criterion: Every audit or dispute-resolution process references DTI-Day.

requirements.title: Reproduce first January test vector
requirements.interpretation: Compare implementation results for 2026-01-01 with every listed value. Section 9 requires exact reproduction and classifies any mismatch as a protocol violation.
requirements.criterion: For 2026-01-01, JDN = DTI-Day = 2461042, DY = 6836, DOY = 83, and canonical = DY6836-083.

requirements.title: Reproduce second January test vector
requirements.interpretation: Compare implementation results for 2026-01-02 with every listed value. Any mismatch is a protocol violation under Section 9.
requirements.criterion: For 2026-01-02, JDN = DTI-Day = 2461043, DY = 6836, DOY = 84, and canonical = DY6836-084.

requirements.title: Reproduce nineteen seventy test vector
requirements.interpretation: Compare implementation results for 1970-01-01 with every listed value. Any mismatch is a protocol violation under Section 9.
requirements.criterion: For 1970-01-01, JDN = DTI-Day = 2440588, DY = 6779, DOY = 149, and canonical = DY6779-149.

requirements.title: Reproduce year two thousand vector
requirements.interpretation: Check exact equality with the printed vector, whose mismatch is declared a protocol violation. This condition is decidable but contradicts the arithmetic and canonical code, which yield DY 6809, DOY 306, and DY6809-306 for the listed JDN.
requirements.criterion: For 2000-01-01, the printed vector requires JDN = DTI-Day = 2451545, DY = 6815, DOY = 26, and canonical = DY6815-026.

requirements.title: Apply canonical Gregorian conversion arithmetic
requirements.quote:
a = (14 - month) // 12
    y = year + 4800 - a
    m = month + 12 * a - 3
requirements.interpretation: Reproduce the forward conversion function using Python floor-division semantics. This specifies the arithmetic underlying Section 6.1 but does not add validation for invalid Gregorian dates.

requirements.title: Apply canonical inverse conversion arithmetic
requirements.interpretation: Reproduce the inverse conversion function with its preceding intermediate values and Python floor division. The text provides no explicit supported JDN range.

requirements.title: Freeze reference date object fields
requirements.quote:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DikenocraticDate:
requirements.interpretation: The canonical Python reference class prevents ordinary reassignment of instance fields after construction. This is a property of the reference object, not an explicit requirement that all stored records be immutable.
requirements.criterion: Ordinary reassignment of fields on a constructed DikenocraticDate instance is rejected.

requirements.title: Raise reference day validation error
requirements.interpretation: Check that constructing the canonical reference object with an out-of-range integer DOY raises the specified ValueError. The reference range check does not independently enforce the integer type annotation.
requirements.criterion: For integer DOY outside [1, 360], construction raises ValueError with message "DOY must be in 1..360".
